literal: When Gun passed seventy, the whole household kept to quiet; in hand he held the classics, collating deviations and errors, loving men of worth, skilled at drawing them on without weariness—the scholarly class for this held him high.
idiomatic: Past seventy, Gun kept his whole household in quiet; he held the classics in hand, collated what had gone astray, delighted in men of talent, and guided them without tiring—the learned held him in high esteem for it.

literal: In the second year of Yongxing his illness grew grave; he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant is a mediocre man, his will without special constancy; it fell to me to live when the Founding Ancestor received Heaven's mandate and the world first opened—I shared in the mist of war at the beginning and galloped through the season of revolution, trusting my wings to the Deng grove and my scales to the deep sea; thus I bore favor and grace, glory reaching within and without.
idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing his illness turned grave; he submitted a memorial: "I am a mediocre man without special resolve, yet I lived when the Founding Ancestor received Heaven's mandate and the world first opened. I shared the war-mist at the start and rode through the season of revolution, trusting my wings to the sacred grove and my scales to the deep sea, and so bore favor whose glory reached within and without the court.

literal: When Your Majesty ascended the dragon throne, I still took part in counsel, yet never offered the slightest sincerity—dust piled like mountains, dew spread like seas.
idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne I still sat in counsel, yet never offered the slightest sincerity—my debt piled like mountains, my thanks spread like seas.

literal: Now my old illness lingers on, my strength empty and spent; Heaven punishes the guilty—I am about to fill the gully and ditch.
idiomatic: Now my old illness lingers and my strength is spent; Heaven punishes guilt, and I am about to fill a ditch.

literal: Yet the dog and horse love their master—I dare not withhold my words.
idiomatic: Yet dog and horse love their master, and I dare not withhold my words.

literal: At present the central lands are at peace, yet the nine regions are not one; in the west are unsubmissive Qiang, in the south rebels who defy command; Min and Shu have other customs, Liao and the sea other teachings.
idiomatic: The central lands are at peace, yet the nine regions are not one: unsubmissive Qiang in the west, rebels in the south, other customs in Min and Shu, other faiths along Liao and the sea.

literal: Though Heaven has raised a bright sage who sets disorder aright and rides the times, to seize the moment and soothe the conjunction truly requires strategy.
idiomatic: Though Heaven has raised a bright sage to set disorder aright and ride the times, seizing the moment and steering events still demands strategy.

literal: The hinge is easily lost; achievement lies in human counsel.
idiomatic: The hinge slips easily; achievement rests on human counsel.

literal: I bow and wish that sagely Way be restored and lofty, that virtue's heart be broadened, so yielding and arms are set forth together, civil virtue and martial achievement both put in motion—then the transformation of great peace and the beauty of "How grand!" would rise again in our day, not only in former ages.
idiomatic: I beg that the sagely Way be lifted high and the heart of virtue broadened, so courtesy and arms stand together and civil and martial power move as one—then the age of great peace and the cry of "How grand!" would rise again today, not only in ages past.

literal: Of old, when Zi Nang was near death, he left word to defend Ying;
idiomatic: Of old, when Zi Nang was near death, he left word to defend Ying; (record).

literal: when Xun Yan took leave of breath, his regret remained in Qi.
idiomatic: when Xun Yan drew his last breath, his regret still lay in Qi.

literal: Your servant, though dim and weak, dares not forget the former resolve; if my soul has spirit, I shall tie grass in the springs below.
idiomatic: I am dim and weak, yet dare not forget that resolve; if my soul has spirit, I shall tie grass in the land below."

literal: " Several days later he died, aged seventy-two.
idiomatic: Several days later he died, aged seventy-two.

literal: Later the Shizu emperor, recording old merit, sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with a patent enfeoffing him posthumously as Grand Mentor and titling him Duke Wenkang.
idiomatic: Later Emperor Shizu, recording old merit, sent the Grand Herald to his tomb with a patent making him Grand Mentor posthumously and titling him Duke Wenkang.

literal: His son Wen was Outer Metropolitan Food Officer and Administrator of Guangning.
idiomatic: His son Wen served as Outer Metropolitan Food Officer and Administrator of Guangning.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Erxing was Administrator of Changli.
idiomatic: His son Erxing was Administrator of Changli — so the record runs.

literal: Wen's younger brother Kai was a provincial chief clerk.
idiomatic: Wen's younger brother Kai was a provincial chief clerk — so the record runs.

literal: His son Dan was learned and principled, his nature especially refined and upright.
idiomatic: His son Dan was learned and principled, his nature especially refined and upright — so the record runs.

literal: At first he was summoned together with Gao Yun; later he was made Secretariat Gentleman, Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, and General Who Establishes Might.
idiomatic: At first he was summoned together with Gao Yun; later he was made Secretariat Gentleman, Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, and General Who Establishes Might — so the record runs.

literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng.
idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng — so the record runs.

literal: Gun's second son Du, in youth ambitious and high-minded, inherited the fief as Marquis of Linwei.
idiomatic: Gun's second son Du, ambitious from youth, inherited the fief as Marquis of Linwei.

literal: Administrator of Shanggu; he entered court as tutor to the Prince of Wuchang.
idiomatic: He was Administrator of Shanggu, then entered court as tutor to the Prince of Wuchang.

literal: He was further made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, commissioned with the staff of authority as Commander over military affairs of Youzhou's Guangyang and Anle commanderies, General Who Pacifies the East, Metropolitan Commander of Qicheng, then transferred as Metropolitan Commander of Helong—wherever he served he won renown.
idiomatic: He was further made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, then commissioned with the staff of authority as commander over military affairs of Youzhou's Guangyang and Anle, General Who Pacifies the East, Metropolitan Commander of Qicheng, then transferred to Metropolitan Commander of Helong—wherever he served he won renown.

literal: Returning to court he became Metropolitan Food Officer of the Central Capital.
idiomatic: On returning to court he became Metropolitan Food Officer of the Central Capital.

literal: He died; posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Ji, titled Marquis Kang.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Ji, titled Marquis Kang.

literal: His son Ling inherited the fief.
idiomatic: His son Ling inherited the fief — so the record runs.

literal: Later he was Metropolitan Director of Works at Chicheng.
idiomatic: Later he was Metropolitan Director of Works at Chicheng — so the record runs.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Zhuang inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zhuang inherited — so the record runs.

literal: He was a Palace Scribe.
idiomatic: He was a Palace Scribe — so the record runs.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Fa inherited.
idiomatic: His son Fa inherited — so the record runs.

literal: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era, by precedent the rank was reduced to marquis — so the record runs.

literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he was made garrison commander of Huaihuang at Jincheng.
idiomatic: In Emperor Shizong's time he was made garrison commander of Huaihuang at Jincheng — so the record runs.

literal: Ling's younger brother Yan was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Left General, and Minister of the Storehouses.
idiomatic: Ling's younger brother Yan was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, Left General, and Minister of the Storehouses — so the record runs.

literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Yongning.
idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Yongning — so the record runs.

literal: Yan's younger brother Bai Ze,[2] at eleven years, met his mother's death; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Bai Ze[2], at eleven, lost his mother; in mourning he was famed for filial piety.

literal: Emperor Shizu heard of it and commended him.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizu heard of it and commended him — so the record runs.

literal: Grown, he loved learning and was broadly versed, keen in affairs of the day.
idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning, was broadly versed, and keen in affairs of the day.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was made Palace Scribe, then moved to Attendant of the Palace Bureau, and was greatly favored and trusted, taking part in secret counsel.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign he was made Palace Scribe, then Attendant of the Palace Bureau, greatly favored and trusted and drawn into secret counsel.

literal: Later the Rouran raided the border; Emperor Xianzu summoned the ministers to discuss it.
idiomatic: Later the Rouran raided the border; Emperor Xianzu summoned the ministers to discuss it — so the record runs.

literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Muchén advanced and said: "If the imperial carriage goes in person, I fear the capital will be shaken with alarm; better to hold steady and secure oneself by defense.
idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Muchén advanced and said: "If Your Majesty goes in person, the capital may panic; better to hold steady and keep to defense.

literal: The foe has driven deep with an army on the march; their grain cannot follow—by my reckoning they will withdraw before long; send generals in pursuit and crushing them is certain."
idiomatic: The enemy has marched deep with no grain to follow; by my reckoning they will soon withdraw—send generals in pursuit and victory is certain."

literal: Bai Ze said: "Your Majesty, reverent and bright as Heaven, treads the tracks of former sages, yet these fools of the wilds in their ignorance lightly violate the royal plan.
idiomatic: Bai Ze said: "Your Majesty, reverent and bright as Heaven, treads the tracks of former sages, yet these wild fools in their ignorance lightly violate the royal plan.

literal: The raiders toil in distant schemes while our generals feast in nearby peril—measured by divine strategy, that cannot be so.
idiomatic: The raiders toil in distant schemes while our generals feast amid nearby danger—measured by divine strategy, that cannot stand.

literal: If now the imperial carriage moves in person, the bandits will surely scatter at the sight of the banners—how could we bear to let divine arms be checked and sit idle while the foe goes free?
idiomatic: If the imperial carriage moves now, the bandits will scatter at the banners—how could we let divine arms be checked and sit idle while the foe escapes?

literal: The honor of ten thousand chariots, besieged in its own walls—advancing, you lose a chance that can be seized; retreating, you fall short of the way of pressing forward without rival. I beg Your Majesty to ponder this."
idiomatic: The honor of ten thousand chariots, walled up at home—advance and you lose a chance that can be seized; retreat and you fall short of pressing forward without rival. I beg Your Majesty to ponder this."

literal: Emperor Xianzu followed this counsel and thereupon utterly broke the barbarian host.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu followed this counsel and utterly broke the barbarian host.

literal: Bai Ze's original name was Zhongkui; Emperor Xianzu bestowed the name Bai Ze and took his daughter into the inner palace as a consort.
idiomatic: Bai Ze's original name was Zhongkui; Emperor Xianzu bestowed the name Bai Ze and took his daughter into the inner palace as a consort — so the record runs.

literal: Sent out as Inspector of Yong Province, he kept his heart clear and his desires few; officials and people were at peace under him.
idiomatic: Sent out as Inspector of Yong Province, he kept his heart clear and his desires few; officials and people were at peace under him — so the record runs.

literal: Emperor Xianzu decreed that any supervising official who in his jurisdiction received one sheep or one jar of wine would be guilty of a capital offense, and the giver would be judged as an accomplice.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu decreed that any supervising official who in his jurisdiction received one sheep or one jar of wine would face capital punishment, and the giver would be judged as an accomplice.

literal: Whoever reported and proved guilt among those from the Masters of Writing downward would be given office according to the weight of the official denounced.
idiomatic: Whoever reported and proved guilt among officials from the Masters of Writing downward would receive office according to the rank of the official denounced.

literal: Bai Ze submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "I bow and have seen the edict forbidding gifts to those from the Masters of Writing downward on pain of bodily punishment, with the accuser to take the denounced man's post.
idiomatic: Bai Ze submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have seen the edict that punishes Masters of Writing and below who accept gifts with death, and gives the accuser the denounced man's post.

literal: I reflect that the triennial review of achievement, demoting and promoting the hidden and the clear, is an unchanging statute and the common pattern of a hundred kings.
idiomatic: I reflect that the triennial review of achievement, demoting the obscure and promoting the clear, is an unchanging statute and the common pattern of a hundred kings.

literal: Today's Metropolitan Bureau is the public ministers of old; all assist in the myriad affairs, praise and harmonize the hundred duties—through them custom is leveled and the way of rule made tranquil.
idiomatic: Today's Metropolitan Bureau is the public ministers of old; all assist in the myriad affairs and harmonize the hundred duties—through them custom is leveled and the way of rule made tranquil.

literal: Even Zhou's lowest officers still had substitute fields for their labor—how much more the honored offices of our dynasty, serving diligently yet receiving no reward; can this be called inheriting Yao and Shun and taking Wen and Wu as one's model?"
idiomatic: Even Zhou's lowest officers still had substitute fields for their labor—how much more our honored offices, serving diligently yet unrewarded; can this be called inheriting Yao and Shun and taking Wen and Wu as one's model?"

literal: If the penalty of sheep and wine is carried out without end, I fear schemers will watch for their chance and loyal ministers slacken in constancy.
idiomatic: If the penalty of sheep and wine goes on without end, I fear schemers will watch for their chance and loyal ministers will slacken.

literal: Yet you wish affairs quiet and the people at peace, government clear and tasks simple—yet entrusting responsibility and demanding results, the lower people are hard put to argue.
idiomatic: Yet you wish affairs quiet and the people at peace, government clear and tasks simple—yet in entrusting responsibility and demanding results, the lower people are hard put to argue.

literal: [3] By my foolish reckoning, I ask that the old laws and statutes be followed, checked against former canons, salaries paid to reward integrity, the disorderly crowd removed first, and ordinary punishments never pardoned.
idiomatic: [3] By my foolish reckoning, I ask that the old laws be followed, checked against former canons, salaries paid to reward integrity, the disorderly crowd removed first, and ordinary punishments never pardoned.

literal: If this can be done, the track of ascending peace may be looked for within a month, and the wind of laying aside punishments will surely arrive in three years."
idiomatic: If this can be done, the track of ascending peace may be looked for within a month, and the wind of laying aside punishments will arrive in three years."

literal: Emperor Xianzu accepted it.
idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu accepted it — so the record runs.

literal: At the beginning of Taihe, more than thirty men of Huai Province led by Yi Qigou plotted rebellion and meant to kill the inspector.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe, more than thirty men of Huai Province led by Yi Qigou plotted rebellion and meant to kill the inspector — so the record runs.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming wished to execute the whole city's people.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming wished to execute the whole city's people — so the record runs.

literal: Bai Ze remonstrated, saying: "I have heard that Heaven loves the life of things and the bright king values the people's lives; therefore to kill one man and take the realm is not what the benevolent do.
idiomatic: Bai Ze remonstrated: "I have heard that Heaven loves the life of things and the bright king values the people's lives; to kill one man and take the realm is not what the benevolent do.

literal: Moreover the Zhou Documents say that father, son, and brothers do not share guilt for one another's crimes; now the ringleaders run wild and are torn apart and put to the sword, yet the whole city is innocent—how can extreme punishment reach so far?
idiomatic: Moreover the Zhou Documents say father, son, and brothers do not share one another's guilt; now the ringleaders are torn apart and put to the sword, yet the whole city is innocent—how can extreme punishment reach so far?

literal: Do not wrong ten households—how much more a whole province; there may be loyal men or benevolent men among them; if excessive punishment sweeps them in, killing the loyal and the benevolent, this is why the Western Earl sighed over the Nine Marquises and Confucius turned his carriage at the river.
idiomatic: Do not wrong ten households—how much more a whole province; there may be loyal or benevolent men among them; if excessive punishment sweeps them in and kills the loyal and benevolent, this is why the Western Earl sighed over the Nine Marquises and Confucius turned his carriage at the river.

literal: I bow and reflect that sagely virtue is bright as a mirror and water-polished by former ritual,[4] restraining sudden wrath and checking thunder's might—then all under Heaven would know fortune."
idiomatic: I beg you to consider that sagely virtue is bright as a mirror and water-polished by former ritual,[4] restraining sudden wrath and checking thunder's might—then all under Heaven would know fortune."

literal: Of old King Li stopped the people's mouths and at last extinguished the house of Ji;
idiomatic: Of old King Li stopped the people's mouths and at last extinguished the house of Ji; (record).

literal: King Wen listened to cart-songs and in the end crushed mighty Chu.
idiomatic: King Wen listened to cart-songs and in the end crushed mighty Chu — so the record runs.

literal: I wish that you not reject words because of the speaker—leave your mind to examine them."
idiomatic: I wish you not reject words because of the speaker—leave your mind to examine them."

literal: The Empress Dowager followed this.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager followed this — so the record runs.

literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and promoted to Director of the Palace Bureau — so the record runs.

literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he died; an edict granted a thousand bolts of silk and three thousand shi of grain, sent a attendant censor to oversee the funeral, and by patent enfeoffed him posthumously as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Xiang, and Duke of Guangping, titled Jian.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he died; an edict granted a thousand bolts of silk and three thousand shi of grain, sent an attendant censor to oversee the funeral, and by patent enfeoffed him posthumously as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Xiang, and Duke of Guangping, titled Jian.

literal: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian.
idiomatic: His eldest son Lun, styled Tiannian — so the record runs.

literal: Past ten years of age, he attended at the ruler's side.
idiomatic: Past ten, he attended at the ruler's side.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Guard Army, Outer Attendant, then Vice Director of the Grand Granary and Grand Rectifier of Yan Province.
idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Guard Army, Outer Attendant, then Vice Director of the Grand Granary and Grand Rectifier of Yan Province — so the record runs.

literal: In the Xiping era the Rouran ruler Chounu sent envoys to court with a letter treating the state as an equal power and without the courtesy due a subject.
idiomatic: In the Xiping era the Rouran ruler Chounu sent envoys to court with a letter treating the state as an equal and without subject courtesy.

literal: Court discussion wished to follow the Han precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply.
idiomatic: Court discussion wished to follow the Han precedent in answering the Xiongnu and send envoys in reply — so the record runs.

literal: Lun submitted a memorial, saying:
idiomatic: Lun submitted a memorial:

literal: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity divided the land and regulated things, distinguished the chief districts, and lands of distant wilds were outside what government could reach.
idiomatic: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity divided the land and regulated things, distinguished the chief districts, and distant wilds lay outside what government could reach.

literal: Therefore ritual has the text of a single audience, and the Documents record the matter of loose reins.
idiomatic: Therefore ritual has the text of a single audience, and the Documents record the matter of loose reins — so the record runs.

literal: The Founding Ancestor, with divine martial bearing and sagely bright design, laid out the imperial plan day by day without rest; thus a stripling's wandering soul was left on one side—also because the central lands had many troubles and urgency lay with the Hua while the Yi and Di could wait.
idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor, with divine martial bearing and sagely design, laid out the imperial plan day by day without rest; thus a stripling's wandering soul was left on one side—also because the central lands had many troubles and urgency lay with the Hua while the Yi and Di could wait.

literal: Gaozu shed light on the central land and his enterprise towered for generations; he shook thunder's might and roused the bear-and-tiger hosts, yet was campaigning south and had no leisure to march north.
idiomatic: Gaozu shed light on the central land and his enterprise towered for generations; he shook thunder's might and roused the bear-and-tiger hosts, yet was campaigning south and had no leisure to march north — so the record runs.

literal: Of old, when the old capital flared with alarm, barbarian envoys were at the suburbs; the sovereign gripped his sword and the imperial letter did not go forth.
idiomatic: Of old, when the old capital flared with alarm, barbarian envoys were at the suburbs; the sovereign gripped his sword and the imperial letter did not go forth — so the record runs.

literal: Emperor Shizong plotted within the tent and opened the borders, raising banners; wherever robe and cap reached, boat and cart ran ten thousand li.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizong plotted within the tent and opened the borders, raising banners; wherever robe and cap reached, boat and cart ran ten thousand li — so the record runs.

literal: At that time the ugly sort knocked at the gate, and the sovereign too followed the honored departed will.
idiomatic: At that time the barbarians knocked at the gate, and the sovereign too followed the honored departed will.

literal: Now great brightness faces the court, grace reaches the traveling reed; the state is rich, the army strong, and those who can speak come to duty.
idiomatic: Now great brightness faces the court, grace reaches the traveling reed; the state is rich, the army strong, and those who can speak come to duty — so the record runs.

literal: What is there to fear in doing this, what is sought in acting thus?
idiomatic: What is there to fear in doing this, what is sought in acting thus? (record).

literal: In former days Xiao Yan sent envoys seeking peace with sincere respect; because his sincerity was not pure, it was suppressed and not granted.
idiomatic: In former days Xiao Yan sent envoys seeking peace with sincere respect; because his sincerity was not pure, it was suppressed and not granted — so the record runs.

literal: The former emperor cast off arms before, and Your Majesty treats the Yi after—will this not be above against Gaozu's heart and below against Shizong's intent?
idiomatic: The former emperor cast off arms before, and Your Majesty treats the Yi after—will this not be above against Gaozu's heart and below against Shizong's intent? (record).

literal: Moreover, though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us; awe them with strength and they may at once submit; show them weakness and covetous watching may arise—the Spring and Autumn Annals calls this "taking us as the augury."
idiomatic: Moreover, though the barbarians admire virtue, they also come to observe us; awe them with strength and they may at once submit; show them weakness and covetous watching may arise—the Spring and Autumn Annals calls this "taking us as the augury." (record).

literal: Again, petty men are hard to approach and the Yi and Di have no kinship; keep them distant and they resent, draw them close and they insult—this has long been their way.
idiomatic: Again, petty men are hard to approach and the Yi and Di have no kinship; keep them distant and they resent, draw them close and they insult—this has long been their way — so the record runs.

literal: Therefore Gaozu and Shizong knew it was so: when they came, they did not press intimacy; when they went, they did not pursue.
idiomatic: Therefore Gaozu and Shizong knew it was so: when they came, they did not press intimacy; when they went, they did not pursue — so the record runs.

literal: The meaning of not making one rule lies here.
idiomatic: The meaning of not making one rule lies here — so the record runs.

literal: Only when they come with tribute of jade and silks and bend the knee in the rites of the frontier may their labor be richly rewarded and their goods entered in the register.
idiomatic: Only when they come with tribute of jade and silks and bend the knee in the rites of the frontier may their labor be richly rewarded and their goods entered in the register — so the record runs.

literal: As for the king's man sent on distant service, bearing command in the barbarian court, honored with the standing of an equal and further given the favor of mutual regard—I fear it will only breed barbarian insolence and do the holy court no good.
idiomatic: As for the king's man sent on distant service, bearing command in the barbarian court, honored as an equal and further given the favor of mutual regard—I fear it will only breed barbarian insolence and do the holy court no good.

literal: Suppose one chose the multitude and raised a worthy envoy, lent the eloquence of Li Yiji, let loose the words of Zhong Jun, leaned on the carriage rail to bring Qi down, and with a long tassel bound Yue—if it differed from former times, one would still be unwilling; how much less exalt them to the utmost honor and extend them feast and friendship?
idiomatic: Suppose one chose the multitude and raised a worthy envoy, lent the eloquence of Li Yiji, let loose the words of Zhong Jun, leaned on the carriage rail to bring Qi down, and with a long tassel bound Yue—if it differed from former times, one would still be unwilling; how much less exalt them to utmost honor and extend them feast and friendship?

literal: Your servant, though low and foolish, still dares to hold firm.
idiomatic: I am low and foolish, yet still dare to hold firm.

literal: If the matter cannot be avoided, there should be issued an imperial edict showing the upper and lower etiquette, and the chief minister should send a letter admonishing them in the way of returning to obedience.
idiomatic: If the matter cannot be avoided, an imperial edict should show the etiquette of superior and inferior, and the chief minister should send a letter admonishing them in the way of returning to obedience.
